chapter_note: This chapter contains a strong, dominant substrate layer organized around two major teaching units: (1) the transmission of the Ambassador's image through Sin/Matter to the rulers who shaped Adam and Eve (¶1-4), and (2) the faculty-storehouse system of the body (¶6-24, 27-28), which is one of the most systematic body-cosmos correspondences in the Kephalaia. The faculty-storehouse teaching maps five senses to five faculties, each with internal storehouses and repositories, governed by the heart-faculty. This is followed by a gates/watchmen correspondence mapping body orifices to a fortified camp. The Light Mind's entry and transformation of the body's systems completes the cosmological architecture. Editorial additions are light: dialogue frame attributions (easily stripped), one pedagogical summary closure (¶5), one editorial bridge applying the transformation teaching to institutional Manichaean worship practices (¶26), and a final exhortation (¶29). The chapter shows mild editorial fatigue in ¶25-26 where worldly examples and institutional vocabulary enter the application of the faculty transformation. Gardner notes the unusual shift from 'Light Mind' to 'Holy Spirit' terminology in ¶28.

paragraphs.core_text: All [these a]bortions, amongst them are Saklas and his consort and the ones whom they have served [ ... ], they are the ones that shaped Adam and Eve. How did they find this beautiful image laid over their shape, even though when it was displayed to their fathers they were not in existence? They never saw the image of the Ambassador! And how did they take the seal of the image of the Ambassador? They added it to [the] shape of Adam and Eve.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: '[Once again the] disciples questioned the enlightener. They say to him:' — formulaic disciple question attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Substantive cosmological question about the transmission of the Ambassador's image through the generations of archons. The question defines the teaching topic — how cosmic image-transmission works across the ruler hierarchy. This is the Persian pedagogical tradition: the question IS the teaching structure.

paragraphs.core_text: The Sin that spurted out from the rulers, which is Matter, shot up [tow]ards the image of the Ambassador. It was cut off from [tha]t place and came down to the earth, for they did not accept [it wi]thin the firmaments. When it came do[wn to] the earth, it formed the tree. It was established within the wood and formed the fruits. And when [the] abortions fell [to] the ground, to the earth, at the [second] time [ ... / ... ]
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'The enlightener [speak]s to them thus:' — formulaic attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Cosmic process teaching: Sin/Matter → saw Ambassador's image → was ejected → descended → formed tree → formed fruits. Classic substrate cosmological narrative. Sin is personified as Matter, functioning as a cosmic agent in a descent-and-formation sequence.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.138⟩
[... in the] fruits, it assumed the[m] and spoke in the ruler, their leader. He says to his companions: Come! Give me your light, and I will construct for you an image aft[er] the likeness of the exalted one. What he said, they did: they gave it to him, and he constructed [ ... ].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Continuation of the cosmic narrative. The ruler's speech to his companions is embedded cosmological dialogue — it describes what the archon IS and DOES within the cosmic architecture. The construction of the image 'after the likeness of the exalted one' is a cosmic process, not citation or application.

paragraphs.core_text: The Sin that s[purted out ... / ... ] which is the Matter that saw the im[age of the Ambassa]dor and that formed the tre[e and was established i]n [i]t; afterwards it came up in the [fruits ... ]. It went in to the rulers [ ... ] they formed Adam and Eve after the [likeness of the] exalt[ed one]. Through the energy of the Sin that had s[een the image of the] Ambassador, it went into the (rulers) [through the fruits. It] assumed them and they [t]oo sculp[ted ... they] begat each of them according to his destiny [ ... ]; one he resembles, one he does not resemble.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Again the enlightener says:' — formulaic attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation of the cosmic process with additional detail: Sin/Matter transmits the image through the fruits into the rulers, who then shape beings 'according to his destiny' with varying resemblance. The heavily lacunose text preserves the essential process: image-transmission through Sin → fruits → rulers → formation.

'Behold, I have taught you this lesson' is a pedagogical closure formula bridging the first teaching section (image-transmission) to the second (faculty-storehouses). The summary content restates what was already taught — no new cosmic information. Functions as a session-transition marker.

paragraphs.core_text: The moulder placed in the form of Adam and Eve limbs, outside and within, for perception and activity. He was apportioned house by house. For everything that his perceptions and elements will receive externally there are internal storehouses and repositories and cavities; and what is received in to them is stored in them. Whenever they will be questioned about what is deposited in their internal storehouses, they bring out what they have received within and give it to the questioner who requested it of them.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' — formulaic attribution. The editorial seam flag is a false positive: there is no institutional vocabulary here, and the content is pure faculty-storehouse teaching.
paragraphs.temporal_note: This opens the second and major teaching unit of the chapter: the faculty-storehouse system. 'House by house' apportionment, 'storehouses and repositories and cavities' — this is the systematic body-cosmos architecture. Gardner identifies this as 'essentially a separate kephalaion,' suggesting it was an independent teaching unit incorporated here.

paragraphs.core_text: In this way his faculty [ ... ] outer [limbs] to look at [ ... ] every type with [in ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Heavily lacunose fragment continuing the faculty-storehouse teaching, likely introducing the faculty of sight. Too damaged to determine detailed content but structurally continuous with the preceding and following paragraphs.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.139⟩
Also [the fa]culty of the eyes [has] houses and cavities and repositories and stores within, so that every image it might see, whether good or evil, whether loveable or detestable or lustful, it can receive into its storehouses and repositories. Also, when the faculty of the eyes is pleased to send out the image that it saw and took in, it can go in to its storehouses [at the] time and think and seek [ ... ] and it brings it out [and] gives it to the questioner who requested it and the one who wan[t]ed it—whether it be something from lu[st ... or a]n image of love [or ... / ... something] hateful. And thus shall that faculty (of the eyes) produce and do what it does in each category.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Faculty of sight: the first fully preserved iteration of the five-sense storehouse system. Maps sight → houses/cavities/repositories/stores → reception → storage → retrieval. Both sides of every mapping stay within the body-cosmos architecture. The impersonal, systematic voice is diagnostic of the oldest layer.

paragraphs.core_text: The faculty of the ears has its own storehouses also. Every sound it might receive, whether good or evil, shall be taken in and placed in its houses and inner repositories, and it is guarded in its [ ... ] for a thousand days. After a thousand days, if someone comes and asks that faculty about the sound that it heard [at] this time and took into its storehouses, immediately it [sh]all g[o] into its repositories and seek and review and search after this word, and send it out from where it was first put, the place in which it was kept.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Faculty of hearing: second iteration. Adds the detail 'a thousand days' as a storage duration — a specific quantitative correspondence within the system. The retrieval process is elaborated: seek → review → search → send out. Perfectly systematic, impersonal voice.

paragraphs.core_text: [In] like order, the faculty of scent [s]hall function just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs. Every [o]dour it shall smell it shall take in [to it] and [d]eposit in its inner storehouses. Every time it will be [a]sked by a questioner, it shall go in [ ... ] and [ ... ] storehouse and remember [ ... ] only these things.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Faculty of scent: third iteration. Abbreviated by reference to the preceding faculties ('in like order... just as that of the eyes and that of the auditory organs'). High substrate vocabulary density (11.94) confirms the systematized register.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.140⟩
However, even the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ, have a faculty dwelling in them. Again, that faculty too, of taste, has thus cavities and repositories set apart for it. It too receives these tastes and gathers them in. A[nd] at any moment when someone will ask of a taste, if [ ... ] it shall send it out and remember tha[t] taste. It shall snare and give even the mar[k of] th[a]t taste; give its memory to the qu[est]ioner who asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Faculty of taste: fourth iteration. Notable detail: 'the mouth and the tongue within it, and the taste organ' — precise anatomical mapping. 'The mark of that taste' suggests the storehouse preserves a qualitative signature. Connects to the taste-world mappings identified in the corpus substrate.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, the fac[ul]ty of touch by the hands is also s[o]: When it might touch, touch shall [receive i]ts memory. And it [takes] it in to its inner repository [until] som[eo]ne will ask this faculty for the memory. [Immediately], it shall go in again and bring out the memory of this touch that it made, and give it to whoever asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Faculty of touch: fifth and final iteration. Completes the five-sense enumeration. 'Touch shall receive its memory' — the faculty receives and stores the qualitative memory of contact. The five-fold sense-faculty system is now complete.

paragraphs.core_text: And the faculty of the heart that rules over them all is much the most like this. Every thing that these five faculties will receive and put in store for the faculty of the heart it shall receive and guard. Any time that they will ask for their deposit it shall send out and give every thing that they gave to it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: The governing faculty: the heart rules over all five sense-faculties. This is the capstone of the faculty-storehouse system. 'These five faculties' — explicit enumeration reference. The heart receives from all five, guards their deposits, and returns them on demand. High substrate density (12.9) — the most concentrated substrate paragraph in the chapter.

paragraphs.core_text: For the counsel of the heart is like the king. All the ad[v]isers of his city and the leaders of his a[r]my are placed with him. Any time if his genera[ls] will entreat him for whatever they wish, he shall give them the ad[v]ice and opinion by which they move.
paragraphs.temporal_note: First simile illustrating the heart-faculty: heart as king. King → advisers → generals is a standard correspondential hierarchy mapping governance. Both sides stay within the cosmic architecture: the heart IS the king of the body's internal city. This is not a worldly reference but a cosmic correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text: Furthermore, it is like a cellarman: [Eve]ry thing that will be entrusted to it by them, and given to it, it shall receive and put in separate vessels and places. Any time [ ... / ... ]
paragraphs.temporal_note: Second simile: heart as cellarman/storekeeper. The bridge connective 'Furthermore' is a normal teaching continuation, not an editorial seam — it extends the simile sequence, not an institutional application. 'Separate vessels and places' maps the heart's storage architecture through correspondence.

paragraphs.core_text:
⟨p.141⟩
... in the place that it put it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Fragment continuing from the preceding lacuna. Too damaged for detailed analysis but structurally part of the cellarman simile or the heart-faculty teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: This also is the way of the faculty of the body. The vision that the eyes will see and give to it, and it receives it in, it shall bring out again from the storehouses wherein it had placed it; and give it to whoever asks for it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation: the body-faculty's interaction with the eye-faculty through the storehouse system. 'This also is the way' signals a systematic recapitulation pass through the senses. The teaching structure cycles: first iteration (¶8-12), governing principle (¶13-16), second pass (¶17-19).

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [the] sound that the ears will hear and give to it, and it receives it from them. At any time when someone will ask it for that sound, it shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked it for that sound. It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Recapitulation for the ear-faculty. Note the repetition at the end ('It shall bring out and give the sound of the ears to whoever has asked') — possibly scribal dittography, but preserved as-is per manuscript.

paragraphs.core_text: Again, [the] faculty of smell in this same pattern; and that of taste is of the same [ty]pe. The touch by the han[ds ... / ... ] they shall bring it out in to [ ... / ... ] And whenever they will as[k it] for it, it shall bring it out and gi[ve it].
paragraphs.temporal_note: Abbreviated recapitulation for scent, taste, and touch — 'in this same pattern,' 'of the same type.' The teaching has established its structure sufficiently that the remaining senses can be covered by reference. This is characteristic of systematic substrate teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: Indeed, watchmen are a[t] these doors guarding them, and bolts are fastened on the doors at the hands of the guards that guard them!
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'Once again the enlightener speaks:' — formulaic attribution. The editorial seam flag is a false positive: 'institutional vocabulary' is empty, and the content introduces a new substrate teaching unit (body-gates-watchmen correspondence).
paragraphs.temporal_note: Transitional statement opening the third teaching unit: the watchmen/gates correspondence. Maps body orifices → doors, spiritual entities → watchmen/guards, authority → bolts. Both sides within the cosmic system.

paragraphs.core_text: Just like watchmen guarding a camp with towers and watch-posts. As the holding rooms come out from there and the bolts are upon the gates, the guards control the bolts of the gates while they sit at the entrance [of] the watchposts. So, someone who belongs to their city as a fellow [cit]izen of them, belonging to their country, for him they shall open [the ga]te and receive him in by their will. However, the foreigner who comes they shall prevent, and leave him standing at the gate. They shall not yield to let him enter. Again, another one whom they will receive in, with great trouble before [they] take him in, you shall find many holding rooms [ ... / ... ] that [ ... ] there are a mass [ ... / ... ] them. The number of d[oor] bolts [ ... ] are [ ... ] Whenever someone will wish [ ... ] the bolts at his hand, opens the gate and brings out whoever is hidden within.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Extended camp/gates correspondence. Body → camp, orifices → gates, spiritual entities → guards/watchmen, impressions → citizens/foreigners. The classification of entrants (citizen vs. foreigner) maps what the body admits vs. rejects. All stays within the cosmic architecture — the camp is not a contemporary institution but a correspondence for the body's defensive system.

paragraphs.core_text: This body too is like the mighty camp. And the gates of the camp with their guards are like the orifices and organs of the body. Now, the orifices of the body are of sight, hearing and smell; and they that send out words. There are many sentinels and a mass of guards placed over the limbs of the body, guarding their orifices. And the faculty in it is the directive of the body, the queen of the entire camp; so that whenever it wishes it can open, or when it wishes it can shut.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed dialogue frame: 'The enlightener says:' — formulaic attribution.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Explicates the body-camp correspondence: body → mighty camp, orifices → gates, faculty → 'the queen of the entire camp.' Note the shift from 'king' (¶14) to 'queen' — the governing faculty is gendered feminine here, which may reflect the Coptic translation or an older tradition about the body's internal governance. The correspondence is systematic and both sides stay within the cosmic architecture.

paragraphs.core_text: However, if and wh[en] the Light Mind comes, it shall tu[rn i]n to the orifices of the body. The rulers, who [a]re the door gua[rds], shall h[in]der and restrain it from en[ter]ing. They shall bind the circu[it] of the body so that the foreign[er] can not enter it.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Opens the Light Mind transformation sequence. The rulers who are the body's door guards resist the Light Mind as 'foreigner' — this connects directly to ¶21's camp correspondence (citizen vs. foreigner). Both sides are cosmic: Light Mind → cosmic entity entering; rulers → cosmic guards resisting. Pure process description.

paragraphs.core_text: Nevertheless, the Light Mind by its wisdom and awe and diligence shall hum[ble] the guards who are set at the body's orifices. When it finishes humbling them it shall take fr[o]m them bolts to all the orifices of the body. Now, the orifices that had been opened before to the parades of lust, to receive in the sights of pleasure, to transfer the [wor]ds of the practice of li[f]e's concerns, to receive in the t[astes] of the different foods and unclean meals together with the sin therein; whoever stops receiving th[is] in, his heart and mind shall follow after.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Light Mind's cosmic action: humbles guards → takes bolts → gains control of orifices. The second half describes what the orifices were previously receiving — this maps sense-faculties to their corresponding dark-realm inputs (lust → sight, pleasure → taste, sin in food). 'Unclean meals together with the sin therein' is cosmic teaching about the mixture in matter, not institutional dietary rules. The whole paragraph describes the cosmic process of authority-transfer at the body's gates.

paragraphs.core_text: By the power of the Light Mind that has suffused him and lived in the body he has humbled Lust, the goddess of the body.
paragraphs.removed_material: Removed editorial application: 'So, now, because the bolts to the body of the righteous person are in the hands of the Light Mind within, he is open to receive in all that is pleasing to God' (editorial framing with 'righteous person'); worldly examples about garments of kings woven with gold and garments of silken women (contemporary world references); 'the chosen person' (institutional vocabulary); 'the aspects of divinity and righteousness and humility and scorned clothes are pleasing to him' (editorial application). Retained the cosmological identification of Lust as 'the goddess of the body' — a unique cosmic personification in this chapter.
paragraphs.temporal_note: This paragraph marks the transition from substrate cosmic process to editorial application. The identification of 'Lust, the goddess of the body' is a genuine substrate element — it personifies Lust as a cosmic ruler of the body, mapping entity → domain. But the surrounding material applies the transformation to the 'righteous/chosen person' with worldly examples (garments, gold, pearls, silken women). The editorial voice is clear: it describes what the audience should experience.

Editorial application of the transformation teaching to the ear-faculty. The structure mirrors ¶25 (before/after under Light Mind) but reaches into Manichaean institutional life: 'the sounds of the lessons of righteousness, the words of the psalms and of the prayers, the praise of the hymns and the lessons of truth, and the knowledge of charity.' These are specific worship practices of the community. Institutional vocabulary score (4.46) confirms. The cosmic framework (Light Mind, sounds of lust, words of magic) is used within the editorial application, not as independent teaching.

paragraphs.core_text: [S]imply, all orifices in similar fashion were opening at one time to wickedness, but now have opened to the good. Sin was ruling in the body this time, doing anything it liked, having none in command.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Returns to impersonal cosmic description after the editorial application of ¶25-26. 'Sin was ruling in the body... doing anything it liked, having none in command' — personified Sin as cosmic ruler of the body with no higher authority. The 'but now' marks cosmic sequence (before/after Light Mind), not editorial temporal reference. Both sides stay within the body-cosmos system.

paragraphs.core_text: Yet, [n]ow, authority has been taken from the Sin in the org[ans] of the body. The Living Spirit has become lord over all its limbs. It has bound them with a chain of peace, and sealed them with the seal of truth. It has opened the orifices of the body to the good, and because of this the good enters them through the ears and the eyes. It dwells in the heart. The H[o]ly Spirit reigns. It does all that it pleases. It annuls [the] will of [S]in, the begin-ning and the end. [In contrast], the will of the [Ho]ly Spir[it] comes about, and the purpose of the Light Mind.
paragraphs.temporal_note: Climactic cosmic description: authority transfer from Sin to the Living Spirit/Holy Spirit/Light Mind. Maps cosmic agents → body governance: bound with chain of peace, sealed with seal of truth, orifices opened to good, good enters through ears and eyes, dwells in heart. Gardner notes the unusual terminological shift from 'Light Mind' to 'Holy Spirit' — this could reflect an older layer where the governing entity was named differently, or editorial harmonization with Christian pneumatology. The content remains purely cosmic: entity → body → authority → transformation. Sin is personified ('the will of Sin, the beginning and the end').

Clear exhortation closure. 'About this I tell you my brothers, my loved ones and my limbs' — first-person address to the community with affective vocatives. Imperative commands: 'make yourselves secure,' 'be watchful people,' 'be you prepared.' Eschatological promise: 'your rest will come about.' The content repurposes the body-orifice teaching for moral application: guard your senses against Sin. This is the devotional wrapper appended to the substrate teaching, exactly matching the exhortation pattern identified across the corpus.
